**Question for today:** How did life expectancy change in Estonia, Latvia and Lithuania since 1950?

```{r}
#| label: setup
pacman::p_load(tidyverse, palmerpenguins, here)
```

## 1. Tidy data in one picture

Tidy data follow three rules: each variable is a column, each observation is a row, each value is a cell. The wide table below breaks the first rule: the variable *year* is spread over many columns.

```{r}
#| label: wide
here("data", "gapminder_life_expectancy_wide.csv") |>
  read_csv(show_col_types = FALSE) |>
  filter(name %in% c("Estonia", "Latvia", "Lithuania")) |>
  select(name, `1950`, `1990`, `2023`)
```

**Ask:** How many variables does this table show? Where is the year?

## 2. pivot_longer(): wide to long

Three arguments: `cols` (the columns to stack), `names_to` (the name of the new column that holds the old column names) and `values_to` (the name of the column that holds the values).

```{r}
#| label: long
here("data", "gapminder_life_expectancy_wide.csv") |>
  read_csv(show_col_types = FALSE) |>
  filter(name %in% c("Estonia", "Latvia", "Lithuania")) |>
  select(name, `1950`:`2023`) |>
  pivot_longer(
    cols = `1950`:`2023`,
    names_to = "year",
    values_to = "life_exp",
    names_transform = as.integer
  )
```

`names_transform = as.integer` turns the year from text into a number, so the x axis is numeric.

## 3. Line plot

```{r}
#| label: line
here("data", "gapminder_life_expectancy_wide.csv") |>
  read_csv(show_col_types = FALSE) |>
  filter(name %in% c("Estonia", "Latvia", "Lithuania")) |>
  select(name, `1950`:`2023`) |>
  pivot_longer(
    cols = `1950`:`2023`,
    names_to = "year",
    values_to = "life_exp",
    names_transform = as.integer
  ) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = year, y = life_exp, color = name)) +
  geom_line()
```

## 4. pivot_wider(): long to wide

The opposite move. `names_from` gives the column whose values become column names. `values_from` gives the column that fills the cells. Wide tables suit a reader who compares two columns.

```{r}
#| label: wider
# Mean body mass per species and sex (from class 7), one column per sex
penguins |>
  filter(!is.na(sex)) |>
  group_by(species, sex) |>
  summarize(mean_mass = mean(body_mass_g), .groups = "drop") |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = sex, values_from = mean_mass) |>
  mutate(difference = male - female)
```
